steps: Maintain SQL Server database backups before migration
Keep previous Docker images tagged and available

Configure ALB for traffic shifting between versions

framework: System.Web namespace removed - requires refactoring HTTP context access
OWIN replaced with ASP.NET Core middleware - authentication flows need updates
Web.config replaced with appsettings.json - configuration access patterns change
Global.asax removed - application lifecycle events move to Program.cs
HttpPostedFileBase replaced with IFormFile - file upload code needs updates
entityFramework: Fluent API syntax changes (HasRequired → HasOne, WillCascadeOnDelete → OnDelete)
String-based Include() discouraged, use strongly-typed ThenInclude()
DbContext constructor changes to accept DbContextOptions
Database initializer pattern replaced with migrations and seed data
database: SQL Server to PostgreSQL - data type mappings required
Case-sensitive queries in PostgreSQL - code may need adjustments
Different date/time functions - verify LINQ translations
Concurrency token handling different (timestamp → xmin or manual version)
hosting: IIS replaced with Kestrel - hosting model fundamentally different
Windows paths to Linux paths - ensure cross-platform path handling
File permissions model different on Linux
Environment variable configuration instead of registry/IIS
Systemd service management instead of Windows services

performance: Kestrel typically faster than IIS for many workloads
PostgreSQL can outperform SQL Server for read-heavy workloads
cost: Smaller Docker images (Linux vs Windows containers)
ECS Fargate pricing typically lower than EC2 Windows instances
scalability: Better suited for microservices if needed in future
development: Better tooling and IDE support for .NET Core/8
maintenance: More frequent updates and security patches
